title: United States and Germany agree to send Abrams and Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine
body:
On Wednesday, 25 January 2023, President Joe Biden announced that the United States would send 31 M1 Abrams tanks to Ukraine, enough to equip one Ukrainian tank battalion. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin, who recommended the move, and Secretary of State Antony Blinken stood with him. The 400 million dollar package included 120 mm rounds and other ammunition, eight tactical vehicles to tow the 70-ton tanks, support vehicles and equipment, and funding for training, maintenance and sustainment.

The Pentagon had previously resisted the move, citing concerns that Ukraine would struggle to operate and maintain the Abrams. The decision came after Germany agreed to let European allies send Leopard tanks. Berlin planned to send one company of Leopard 2 A6 tanks, totalling 14, and allies collectively planned to send nearly 90 tanks, enough for two battalions. Biden denied that Berlin had forced his change of position. The United Kingdom's Challenger 2 tank was among the armoured vehicles Western officials had offered Ukraine in the weeks before.

U.S. officials said a training programme would cover operating the tanks and integrating them into manoeuvre operations. Delivery was expected to take months rather than weeks, because the tanks would come at the end of a months-long contracting process and the Pentagon had to resolve logistics, including supplying the jet fuel the Abrams uses. The tanks were meant to help Ukraine defend against an expected Russian offensive in spring and to support efforts to retake territory.
